blocks.name: register_file
blocks.responsibility: Provide 32 32-bit integer registers with asynchronous reads, synchronous writes, asynchronous active-high reset, and hardwired-zero x0.
blocks.design_rationale: Isolates register state and x0 behavior, making reset and writeback timing straightforward to verify.

blocks.name: alu
blocks.responsibility: Compute RV32I arithmetic, logic, shifts, and comparisons, plus all RV32M multiply, divide, and remainder results. Provide equality, signed-less-than, and unsigned-less-than flags for branch decisions.
blocks.design_rationale: Centralizes arithmetic and comparison datapaths, simplifying operation-level verification and avoiding duplicated hardware.

blocks.name: control_unit
blocks.responsibility: Decode the instruction into ALU, register-write, memory, writeback, and control-flow signals. Select conditional branches using the ALU comparison flags.
blocks.design_rationale: Keeps instruction decoding and control-flow decisions separate from datapath state, improving conformance review and testability.

blocks.name: cpu
blocks.responsibility: Implement the single-cycle RV32IM processor, instantiate the register file, ALU, and control unit, generate the PC and immediates, perform load extraction and extension, and drive the instruction and data buses.
blocks.design_rationale: Keeps the required external contract in one top-level entity while allowing each major datapath function to be verified independently.

notes: Use VHDL-2008 with only ieee.std_logic_1164 and ieee.numeric_std. The CPU generates sign-extended I, S, B, and J immediates and the U immediate, maintains the current PC on instr_addr, and gives JAL/JALR priority over taken branches when selecting the next PC. Data addresses remain byte addresses; loads select bytes or halfwords using the low address bits and apply the required sign or zero extension. alu_imm_sel encodings are 00=I, 01=S, 10=U; wb_sel encodings are 00=ALU, 01=load, 10=PC+4. Define alu_op encodings consistently between control_unit and alu for every RV32I and RV32M operation. RV32M behavior must include division by zero and signed overflow results specified by the RISC-V M extension.
